title: First recurring Monitor learning slice for Anth.us, Papyrus, TI and Pilobolus
description:
## Current delivery status

Implementation remains in progress; production two-layer classification and applied feedback are not complete.

- Public HN collection succeeded at 2026-10-20T11:35:17Z: 30 deduplicated private review sources with separate discovery provenance, mode-0600 queue/checkpoint/export files and presentation deduplication. Collection-only staging is distinct from publication Reference intake and full routing.
- Parent enabled an hourly automation in America/New_York. No first scheduled-run receipt or reliable next-run timestamp has been observed. Parent owns review-batch delivery and scheduled wake coordination; avoid overlapping manual collection.
- Draft PR https://github.com/AnthusAI/Papyrus/pull/382 is pushed, unmerged. Collector head 4a151214 passed Python/TypeScript/smoke CI. Latest guideline/tracker head bbacf15ce703dc620dbcf583c13f1431226c3c5d has CI running; do not describe the latest head as green until verified.
- 50 explicit human decisions and their explanations/message provenance are privately preserved and hash-verified. Zero applied feedback, labels, seeds or training. Individual labels and publication policy prose must not appear in public tracker records.
- Database-guideline propagation is implemented and tested under PPY-6b80ab and PPY-eba9cf: 63 focused Python tests and 24 BDD scenarios/98 steps pass locally with synthetic providers. Source/CLI request evidence is not production deployment or live inference evidence.

## Required architecture and acceptance

The same immutable discovered source revision must be evaluated once by ONE SHARED REMOTE Cyclotron across four publication-relevance outputs. Only relevant outputs continue to each publication's INTEGRATED Cyclotron, with section-fit outputs and its selector. Preserve shared decision identity plus account/publication/output/binding revision and prediction fingerprint. Independent first-stage engines or a local fallback do not satisfy this contract.

Recurring collection -> persisted discovery/Reference provenance -> correctly scoped real shared decision -> integrated section decisions -> human review -> authorized, verified applied feedback is the intended full slice. Never treat predictions, advisory judgments or received JSON feedback as human-label application. Keep evaluation answers separate from seeds and preserve baseline-before-seeding order.

## Exact remaining gates

1. Verify the hourly automation's first actual run and resulting queue receipt.
2. Reconcile and normally release the reviewed shared publication-host composition and trusted model-context adapter. Interactive sign-in was verified, but publication routing/provider composition remains undeployed and classifier execution disabled. No live predictions have run.
3. Verify current account/person/publication grants, shared remote output/binding identities, and each integrated publication's canonical corpus/section bindings. Do not invent namespaces, grants, credentials or predictions.
4. Review/roll out Papyrus context changes through the normal package/consumer pipeline. The existing editorial-checks role source proposes only private reads getEditorialContext and listKnowledgeCorporaByRoleAndName; no production grant was applied. Reconcile current consumer owner changes, including existing provider-secret fixes, rather than duplicating them.
5. Under the correct authenticated publication, read current private mission/policy and section overlays, prepare exact preserved-content diffs, and verify effective context/request provenance. Production policy writes and any live model test require the exact target/scope and a bounded approved provider budget. Do not publish private prompt text in traces or artifacts.
6. Apply received feedback only through the intended authority-bound human-feedback path after correct prediction/output targets and ordering are verified; retain actual applied receipts. No fabricated authority, seeds or synthetic predictions.

Other RSS/headless/source-adapter plans remain design-only unless separately authorized. No merge, infrastructure, publication or deployment action follows from tracker upkeep.

Draft PR: https://github.com/AnthusAI/Papyrus/pull/382 into develop, branch feature/PPY-3212f1-hn-monitor. Implementation commit 2962fc56; architecture correction 81bd5bd2. Not merged or deployed. Prior develop-to-main PR377 is merged; this feature is not in develop/main.

All pending; all private provenance bodies read back with correct HN sourceId/corpusId. No labels, predictions, seed or training applied.

Ryan's final architecture is captured in Monitoring epic PPY-2d77c8, pilot task, behavior PPY-b8b15c and feedback PPY-437a10: one shared REMOTE Cyclotron with distinct Papyrus/TI/Anth.us relevance outputs together on each source, then INTEGRATED per-publication Cyclotrons with section-specific outputs. Both require real end-to-end proof. No local first-stage or independent-model fallback.

Remote connection remains unverified/pending, not denied: exact actual central lab/API endpoint, existing account/role grants and three-output binding are unknown. Current Cyclotron-web main README and infra README state static S3/CloudFront marketing, no application server; main/develop source inventory did not expose hosted API, and both Cyclotron/Cyclotron-web have no open PRs. Core does provide multi-output PublicationLab and HTTPPublicationClient: POST /publications/{publication}/operations, cyclotron-publication/v1, decide with bindingRevision and item id/values; it requires an injected authenticated host/verified actor. This source contract is not deployed proof. Existing Papyrus embedded snapshot is inventory only and was not modified. Per-publication integrated section bindings likewise need verification.

No new persistent access/IAM/infrastructure created. Next real classification must use verified remote host and shared engine, then integrated section engines. Human evaluation labels remain pending and must not seed baseline first. PR367 remains the separate restricted user-session intake/release dependency.
